text:
## Observations

1. The input is a single valid direction code containing one or two letters.
2. Opposite directions swap N with S and E with W.
3. A diagonal code lists its north–south component first and its east–west component second. Taking the opposite changes both letters while preserving their order.

## Solution sketch

> The input is a single valid direction code containing one or two letters.

1. Read one line from standard input and strip surrounding whitespace to obtain the direction code.

> Opposite directions swap N with S and E with W.

2. Replace each letter with its opposite. A cardinal direction needs one replacement, so N becomes S.

> A diagonal code lists its north–south component first and its east–west component second. Taking the opposite changes both letters while preserving their order.

3. Join the replacement letters in their original order and print the result on its own line. For example, SE becomes NW.

> The input is a single valid direction code containing one or two letters.

4. The algorithm processes and stores at most two direction letters, so it uses O(1) time and O(1) extra space.
